Radiology Report
Date: 09/10/2026
Patient: Lance Morar, 72-year-old male

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/10/2026: acute osteoporotic L1 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.
Approximately 44% loss of L1 vertebral body height.
Focal kyphotic deformity at L1 measuring 22 degrees.

Impression:
The imaging demonstrates an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the L1 vertebral body characterized by significant height loss and associated bone marrow edema. There is a focal kyphotic deformity at this level measuring 22 degrees, consistent with the fracture morphology.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be guided by the patient's symptoms and clinical status.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/23/2026
Patient: Lance Morar, 72-year-old male

History:
Back pain began 08/27/2026 after lifting a laundry basket, 4 weeks before this visit. Pain NRS 6/10 despite 3 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and tramadol, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current conservative management and monitor symptoms closely. Consider interventional options if pain persists or worsens.
